group_assessment.weighting: A Shanghai biochemistry and ophthalmology group (from the affiliations) that earlier built a hypoxia-regulated WWOX adenovirus for lung cancer. Primary for WWOX gene therapy in lung cancer cells; not a loss-of-function, neurological or metabolic group. The measurements are a short set of single-line overexpression assays; the pathway attribution in the title is an interpretation.

entries.proposition: The system is transient overexpression of WWOX in one lung adenocarcinoma line; viability falls to about 73 to 86 percent of control (MTT), a modest effect read as anti-proliferative.
entries.snippet: The cell proliferative percentage decreased to 85.62±3.27, 75.47±3.15 and 73.04±1.79% at 24, 48 and 72 h, respectively (Fig. 1).

entries.proposition: The cytochrome c result is a single blot of a cytosolic fraction (10,000 g supernatant) probed for beta-tubulin as loading control; no mitochondrial fraction, mitochondrial marker or purity control is shown, and no inhibitor or knockdown test is applied.
entries.snippet: The analysis revealed a marked elevation in the level of cytosolic cytochrome C of the cells transfected with pcDNA3.0-WWOX compared to that of the control cells (Fig. 3).
entries.anchor: Results, WWOX triggers the release of cytochrome C from mitochondria

entries.proposition: The conclusion that apoptosis is 'mainly' mitochondrial rests on cytochrome c and caspase-9 and -3 cleavage; no extrinsic-pathway readout (caspase-8) or comparison of pathways is reported, so 'mainly' is an interpretation.
entries.snippet: In conclusion, our data show that WWOX is involved in cell apoptosis, mainly through the mitochondrial pathway.

entries.snippet: We therefore speculated that WWOX translocates to the mitochondrion in response to apoptotic stress, affecting the mitochondrial intermembrane stability.
